record.paper_title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations
record.original_question: Given an arbitrary symplectic Lefschetz fibration over S^2, determine whether repeated fiber sum with a suitable collection of standard holomorphic Lefschetz fibrations must eventually produce a fibration that is isomorphic to a holomorphic one.

evidence.quote: Question 2.4. Does every symplectic Lefschetz fibration become isomorphic to a holomorphic fibration after repeatedly fiber summing with certain standard holomorphic fibrations?
Note added in proof: Questions 2.4 and 2.5 have now essentially been solved.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the 2-sphere $S^2$ is a smooth map $f\colon X\to S^2$ from a compact symplectic 4-manifold $(X,\omega)$ whose generic fiber is a smooth symplectic surface of genus $g\ge 0$ and whose finitely many critical points are modeled in local complex coordinates by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto z_1^2+z_2^2$, with the symplectic form restricting nondegenerately to the smooth fibers. Such a fibration is called holomorphic if $X$ admits an integrable complex structure compatible with $\omega$ in which $f$ is holomorphic onto $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Given two Lefschetz fibrations $f_1\colon X_1\to S^2$ and $f_2\colon X_2\to S^2$ of the same fiber genus, their fiber sum $f_1\#_f f_2\colon X_1\#_f X_2\to S^2$ is the Lefschetz fibration obtained by removing tubular neighborhoods of a regular fiber from each $X_i$ and gluing the resulting boundaries by a fiber-preserving diffeomorphism.

Question: Does there exist, for every genus $g$, a finite collection $\mathcal{H}_g$ of holomorphic Lefschetz fibrations of genus $g$ over $S^2$ such that for every symplectic Lefschetz fibration $f\colon X\to S^2$ of genus $g$, after fiber-summing $f$ a sufficient number of times with appropriately chosen members of $\mathcal{H}_g$, the result is isomorphic (as a Lefschetz fibration) to a holomorphic Lefschetz fibration?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been substantially addressed. Auroux's "A stable classification of Lefschetz fibrations" (math/0412120) shows that, for each genus, there is a universal Lefschetz fibration such that any two Lefschetz fibrations with matching numerical invariants become isomorphic after enough fiber sums with it. In genus 2, combined with the Siebert–Tian holomorphicity result for genus-2 Lefschetz fibrations with only irreducible singular fibers, this implies that every genus-2 Lefschetz fibration becomes holomorphic after fiber sum with a suitable holomorphic fibration. Thus the question is essentially resolved in the stable sense (and fully in genus 2), though a complete holomorphicity statement in all genera reduces to further open holomorphicity questions.

status_evidence.title: A stable classification of Lefschetz fibrations
status_evidence.snippet: For each genus there is a universal Lefschetz fibration such that any two Lefschetz fibrations with matching invariants become isomorphic after sufficiently many fiber sums with it.
status_evidence.claim: Stable classification of symplectic Lefschetz fibrations under fiber sums with a standard holomorphic fibration.

status_evidence.title: Fiber sums of genus 2 Lefschetz fibrations
status_evidence.snippet: Using Siebert–Tian holomorphicity for genus-2 fibrations with irreducible fibers, every genus-2 Lefschetz fibration becomes holomorphic after fiber sum with a holomorphic fibration.
status_evidence.claim: In genus 2, the stabilization question is solved positively.
